solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Drop male conservative in disgrace

indicators.note: the conservative sits in the word for disgrace

blocks.note: M = male
odium = public disgrace; it opens to take the C
C = Conservative

explanation.surface: A male Tory is dropped from office amid scandal.
explanation.walkthrough: "Drop" reads as a verb about sacking the man, but it is a noun: a drop, a tiny amount.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a drop of milk is a tiny measure, the same small quantity the Latin-derived word names.

clue.text: Prime minister getting a grip on adolescent disorder

indicators.note: the prime minister's name grips the youth, holding him inside

blocks.note: Theresa May, UK prime minister 2016-19
a lad = a boy, an adolescent; goes inside MAY

explanation.surface: A prime minister tries to take control of unrest among the young.
explanation.walkthrough: Crosswords often use the surname of a recent prime minister; Theresa May led Britain from 2016 to 2019.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the medical sense: an ailment or illness is a disorder of the body.

clue.text: Gathered information about campaign from lawyer involved in Act

indicators.note: the lawyer is placed inside the act

blocks.note: a deed = an act; it opens as DE...ED
a brief is British slang for a barrister or solicitor

explanation.surface: Someone collected facts about a campaign from a lawyer caught up in legislation.
explanation.walkthrough: "Brief" is informal British for a lawyer, especially a defence barrister. "Act" looks like a statute, but it is simply a deed.
explanation.definitionFit: Soldiers and agents are questioned after a mission to gather what they learned on the campaign.

clue.text: Innate evil shown up in man behind bars

indicators.note: in a down clue, "up" turns the word over from bottom to top

blocks.note: core = central, intrinsic, as in core values
ill = evil, as in ill will; turned up to give LLI

explanation.surface: A prisoner reveals the wickedness born in him.
explanation.walkthrough: The "bars" are musical bars, not a prison: Arcangelo Corelli was a baroque composer, so he stands behind his bars of music.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: any composer is the man behind the bars of his music.

clue.text: According to Spooner, fool could take on another role

indicators.note: Spooner swapped the starting sounds of words

blocks.note: a loon is a fool; it takes the M from the next word
might = could; it takes the L from the first word

explanation.surface: A clown might switch parts in a play.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is theatrical, but the role wanted is a second job.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means to work a second job on the side, often at night, taking on another role.

clue.text: Summit briefly going into recess brings calm

definitions.note: The answer is a base verb; the clue's "brings calm" is third person, so read it as "bring calm".

indicators.note: the summit word is cut short by one letter
the shortened summit goes inside the recess

blocks.note: an apse is a vaulted recess in a church; it opens as AP...SE
PEAK without its last letter

explanation.surface: A short summit meeting taken into a parliamentary recess eases tensions.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is diplomatic: a summit and a recess. But the recess is architectural, an apse.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to pacify angry people is to bring calm.

clue.text: First in series of affectations upset teller of tales

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset turns the word upside down, reversing it

blocks.note: A is first in any lettered series: A, B, C
a pose is an affectation; reversed to ESOP

explanation.surface: The first of a string of mannerisms upset a storyteller.
explanation.walkthrough: "First in series" is not the letter S: it is A, first of the series A, B, C.
explanation.definitionFit: The ancient Greek storyteller behind the fables of the tortoise and the hare and the fox and the grapes.

clue.text: Idiot put up flyer in Bay Area?

indicators.note: in a down clue, putting a word up writes it bottom to top

blocks.note: a sap is a fool; put up to PAS
a tern is a seabird

explanation.surface: A fool sends up a bird over San Francisco Bay.
explanation.walkthrough: "Bay Area" suggests San Francisco, but a bay is a brown horse, and the pastern is part of its leg. The question mark flags the definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the part of a horse's foot between fetlock and hoof is one area of a bay.

clue.text: Publicity campaign plugs gift

indicators.note: the campaign fills a gap inside the publicity, as a plug fills a hole

blocks.note: an ad = an advertisement; it opens as A...D
a war is a military campaign

explanation.surface: An advertising drive promotes a present.
explanation.walkthrough: "Plugs" sounds like advertising, which suits the surface, but here it means fills.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a prize or grant is something given, a gift.

clue.text: Deplore what determines senior manager’s salary

blocks.note: an exec = an executive
the thing that sets a salary is its rate
the rate of pay

explanation.surface: Condemn the process that fixes a boss's pay.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is the familiar outrage at boardroom pay, which is exactly what the definition asks you to do.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to denounce or loathe something is to deplore it.

clue.text: Hard financial promises introduced by political party ignoring unions initially

indicators.note: the party name leaves out a letter
only the first letter of unions is dropped
the party comes before the promises

blocks.note: LABOUR without the U of unions
IOUs are written promises to pay

explanation.surface: A political party, sidelining the unions, makes tough spending pledges.
explanation.walkthrough: Labour is Britain's main left-wing party, historically tied to the trade unions, which makes dropping the U neat.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: work demanding great effort is hard.

clue.text: Fish egg’s first to hatch

indicators.note: take only the first letter of egg

blocks.note: the shad is a herring-like fish
first letter of egg

explanation.surface: A fish's egg is the first one to break open.
explanation.walkthrough: "Hatch" means what eggs do, but here it is the artist's hatching: shading with fine lines.
explanation.definitionFit: The drawing sense: to hatch is to darken an area with close parallel lines.

clue.text: Exercise machine that could get boring

blocks.note: a practice routine, as soldiers or fire wardens rehearse
a tool that bores holes

explanation.surface: A gym machine that might become tedious.
explanation.walkthrough: "Boring" means tedious in the surface; the second definition wants it literally, making holes. A fire drill is an exercise.
explanation.definitionFit: One word covers both a repeated practice exercise and the tool that bores holes.

clue.text: Observer of speech by Taoiseach possibly clinging to power in Ireland

indicators.note: the leader wraps around the Irish piece
power goes inside Ireland

blocks.note: the Taoiseach is Ireland's prime minister, one kind of leader; it opens as L...EADER
P (power) inside IR (Ireland)

explanation.surface: Someone watches an Irish prime minister's speech as he hangs on to office.
explanation.walkthrough: The Taoiseach is the Irish prime minister; "possibly" marks him as one example of a leader.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who follows speech by watching the mouth observes it rather than hearing it.

clue.text: Staff appreciate this band appearing in fundraiser for further education

indicators.note: the band sits inside the letters for further education

blocks.note: FE = further education, UK colleges after school; it opens as F...E
a ring is a band, as round a finger
a charity event held to raise money

explanation.surface: Staff love it when a band plays at a charity gig for a college.
explanation.walkthrough: FE is British shorthand for further education, the college sector. "Staff appreciate this" is a descriptive definition: employees like their perks.
explanation.definitionFit: A descriptive definition: a perk on top of pay, such as a company car, is something staff appreciate.

clue.text: Graduate admitting agitated state talked nonsense

indicators.note: the graduate lets the agitated state in

blocks.note: a BEd is a Bachelor of Education; it opens as B...ED
in a lather = worked up

explanation.surface: A graduate confesses to being flustered and spoke rubbish.
explanation.walkthrough: Graduate is usually BA, which leads nowhere; here it is BEd, the teaching degree.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to babble foolishly at length is to talk nonsense.

clue.text: Home runs must be set up in subsequent fixtures?

indicators.note: in a down clue, setting up writes the letters bottom to top
the reversed pair goes inside the word for subsequent

blocks.note: future = to come, subsequent; it opens as FU...TURE
in = at home
R = runs in cricket scoring; IN+R is set up as RNI

explanation.surface: A home run has to be arranged in future matches.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is sport: home runs and fixtures, which are scheduled matches. The question mark allows fixtures to stand loosely for the contents of a house.
explanation.definitionFit: Tables and chairs, like fixtures, are the fittings of a home; the question mark admits the stretch.

clue.text: Period where one might find training difficult?

definitions.text: Period where one might find training difficult?

blocks.note: reads as a span of time, but it is the punctuation mark ending a sentence

blocks.clueFragment: where one might find training difficult?
blocks.note: reads as a hard gym session, but means a station where you cannot board because the train is packed

explanation.surface: A spell of time when working out is hard going.
explanation.walkthrough: "Training" reads as exercise, but think of catching a train: that is hard at a stop where the train is already full.
explanation.definitionFit: The British name for the period that ends a sentence, read cryptically as a stop where trains are full.

clue.text: Subordinate who fails to meet binding targets?

definitions.text: who fails to meet binding targets?

blocks.note: a lowly assistant or underling

blocks.clueFragment: who fails to meet binding targets?
blocks.note: someone whose strapping falls short, split as UNDER plus a strapper

explanation.surface: A junior who keeps missing agreed goals.
explanation.walkthrough: "Binding targets" sounds like firm quotas; the second reading is literal, someone who binds with straps and does too little of it.
explanation.definitionFit: An old word for an inferior agent, and cryptically one who straps below target.

clue.text: Group of potential soldiers in detachment

blocks.note: a body of troops kept back for call-up
aloofness, emotional distance

explanation.surface: A squad of would-be soldiers forms part of a military detachment.
explanation.walkthrough: "Detachment" plays on a military unit, but the sense wanted is coolness of manner.
explanation.definitionFit: One word for standby troops and for restraint of manner.

clue.text: Standard approach exposed vulgar new arrival

indicators.note: stripped of its outer letters, so its middle is laid bare

blocks.note: par = the standard or norm
AVENUE, an approach road, without its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A normal way in reveals a crude newcomer.
explanation.walkthrough: An avenue is a tree-lined approach to a house; removing its outer letters leaves VENU.
explanation.definitionFit: From French for 'arrived': a newly rich upstart thought to lack class.

clue.text: Take in group from failing establishment

indicators.note: a group of letters taken from the phrase

blocks.note: the letters run across the join of the two words

explanation.surface: Absorb a set of people from a collapsing institution.
explanation.walkthrough: "Group" looks like a noun to be defined, but it describes the run of letters lifted from fail-ING EST-ablishment.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to swallow food is to take it in.

clue.text: Key figure in report of Nessie apparently

indicators.note: a report is something spoken

blocks.note: Nessie, the Loch Ness monster, is supposedly the loch's myth

explanation.surface: An important person in an account of the Loch Ness monster.
explanation.walkthrough: Nessie is the legendary monster of Loch Ness in Scotland; a loch is a Scottish lake. "Key figure" means an important person in the surface but is literal here.
explanation.definitionFit: The tradesman who cuts keys is, literally, a key figure.

clue.text: Pious platitudes on love in some poet’s work

indicators.note: in a down clue, the platitudes sit on top of the love

blocks.note: cant = hypocritical, sanctimonious talk
love = zero in tennis, O

explanation.surface: Sanctimonious clichés about love appear in a poet's verse.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface makes love the theme of the poem; it is only the tennis zero.
explanation.definitionFit: A section of a long poem, as in Dante or Byron, is some of a poet's work.

clue.text: University dons involved with part that’s used in programme

definitions.note: Read as "(data) that's used in a programme".

indicators.note: the part puts on the university letter as one dons a coat

blocks.note: in = involved, as in in on the plan
pt = part; it opens as P...T
U = university

explanation.surface: College fellows are engaged with a role in a broadcast.
explanation.walkthrough: "Dons" reads as university teachers, the natural partner of "University", but it is the verb: the part dons (wears) the U.
explanation.definitionFit: The data fed into a computer program is what the program uses.

clue.text: Abdicate, wanting son to be king?

blocks.note: to abdicate is to resign the throne
S = son; removed from RESIGN

explanation.surface: A monarch steps down, wishing his son to take the throne.
explanation.walkthrough: "Wanting" reads as wishing, which is the surface story; its job is lacking.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to rule as monarch is to be king.

clue.text: Several men who serve general purpose

blocks.note: ten stands for several, a handful
OR = other ranks, soldiers who are not officers

explanation.surface: Several soldiers serve a general's purpose.
explanation.walkthrough: "General" looks like an army officer beside the soldiers, but "general purpose" is the gist.
explanation.definitionFit: The general drift or purport of a speech, as in the tenor of his remarks.

clue.text: Harry essentially severed connections with English

blocks.note: per se = in itself, essentially
to cut someone is to snub them, severing ties
E = English

explanation.surface: Prince Harry has effectively cut ties with England.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is Prince Harry stepping back from the royal family; here harry is a verb, to hound.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb harry means to harass relentlessly, hounding a victim.

clue.text: Leader of Parliament set about stopping corruption and dissent

indicators.note: the first letter of Parliament
about means turned round, as in about-turn, so the word runs backwards
the reversed set plugs the corruption

blocks.note: first letter of Parliament
rot = decay, corruption; it opens as RO...T
SET reversed

explanation.surface: The head of Parliament moves to end sleaze and discord.
explanation.walkthrough: "Leader of Parliament" sounds like a political post; it only gives P.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: an objection voiced is dissent.

clue.text: Extremely stubborn Democrat snubbed public support

indicators.note: snub-nosed: the word is cut short at its end

blocks.note: D = Democrat
OUT (public, known) with its tail docked
a rest is a support, as for a cue

explanation.surface: A very obstinate Democrat rejected popular backing.
explanation.walkthrough: "Snubbed" means rebuffed in the surface; its job is docked, like a snub nose. Out = public, as when news is out.
explanation.definitionFit: The superlative of a word for stern and obstinate, so the most stubborn.
